areas.purpose: Reduce crushed bauxite (-25 mm) to a pumpable caustic slurry (100% < 1 mm, P80 ~250-400 um) in hot spent ('mill') liquor, at a controlled bauxite-to-liquor charge, and buffer it ahead of pre-desilication. Grinding exposes gibbsite and kaolinite surfaces so that desilication and the short (30-60 min) low-temperature digestion go to completion, while keeping the residue coarse enough to settle and be washed.
areas.process_description:
1) Blended crushed bauxite (-25 mm top size, ~10 % free moisture, F80 ~10-20 mm - engineering estimate) is reclaimed from the bauxite stockyard (stockpile/reclaim area) by belt conveyor and distributed by a shuttle/tripper to four mill feed bins (3 grinding lines operating + 1 standby, each line rated for ~1/3 of plant feed plus ~10-15 % margin).
2) A weigh-belt feeder under each bin meters ~213 t/h dry (~237 t/h wet) bauxite into the mill feed chute. Hot mill liquor (spent liquor from evaporation: C ~260-290 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C ~0.36-0.38, 75-90 degC) is added in the feed chute in ratio to the dry bauxite rate (ratio controller, bauxite moisture compensated) to give ~50-55 % solids w/w inside the mill. The total bauxite-to-liquor 'charge' across grinding + digestion liquor is the main lever on digester A/C, so the dry feed rate is measured very carefully (weightometer + moisture analyser/ lab moisture).
3) Wet overflow ball mills (nominal 4.4 m dia x 6.5 m EGL, ~2 MW) grind the ore. Hot caustic begins reacting: a small part of the gibbsite dissolves (Al(OH)3 + NaOH -> NaAl(OH)4) and kaolinite (reactive silica) starts dissolving: Al2Si2O5(OH)4 + 6 NaOH -> 2 NaAl(OH)4 + 2 Na2SiO3 + H2O. Temperature rises a few degC from mill power and reaction.
4) Mill discharge passes through a trommel bolted to the discharge trunnion; scats (>~8-12 mm hard caprock, laterite lumps, tramp metal, worn balls) go to a scats bunker. Slurry falls into the mill discharge pump box where extra liquor is added to bring the slurry to ~45-48 % solids for screening.
5) Mill discharge pumps (1 operating + 1 standby per mill, hard-metal centrifugal slurry pumps) lift the slurry to a flow divider feeding multi-deck high-frequency screens (1.0 mm polyurethane panels) located on an elevated screen floor.
6) Screen oversize (circulating load ~80-150 % - engineering estimate) returns by gravity chute to the mill feed chute (closed circuit). Screen undersize (product) flows by gravity launder to two agitated slurry storage tanks (~4-5 h combined surge at design rate) that decouple grinding from pre-desilication/digestion.
7) Slurry transfer pumps deliver ~830 m3/h of slurry (SG ~1.65-1.72, 44-48 % solids, 75-90 degC) to the pre-desilication heaters (A05) at a rate set by the digestion feed demand.
Control philosophy: bauxite dry tph and liquor:bauxite ratio (charge control, fed forward from digestion A/C target), mill power/ sound/ bearing pressure for mill load, pump-box level via VFD on mill discharge pump, product PSD (online analyser + shift sieve), storage tank levels, slurry density (radiometric or Coriolis).
Note for high-temperature (boehmitic) plants: the grinding circuit is essentially the same, but lime is often added at the mill (for titanate scale and phosphate control), and grinding may be finer.

equipment.name: Mill feed bins and weigh-belt feeders
equipment.function: Provide ~2-4 h live surge of crushed bauxite in front of each mill and meter a precisely known dry bauxite rate into the mill (charge control).
equipment.type_selected: Steel mass-flow-profile bin with slotted/ transition hopper, discharging onto a variable-speed weigh-belt feeder (load cell idler + speed sensor).
equipment.why_this_type: Wet, clayey bauxite (8-12 % moisture, fines) is cohesive and prone to rat-holing; a steep/ slotted hopper plus belt feeder (rather than a vibrating feeder) gives reliable flow, and the weigh-belt gives the tph signal needed for caustic-to-bauxite ratio control.
equipment.alternatives: Concrete silos with reclaim belt; apron feeder + separate belt scale; loss-in-weight not used at these rates.
key_dimensions: Bin live capacity ~500-800 t each (2-3 h at 237 t/h) - engineering estimate
Bin ~8-9 m square/ round plan, ~12-15 m high incl. hopper; hopper wall >= 60-70 deg from horizontal - engineering estimate (confirm with Jenike flow-property tests)
Weigh-belt feeder ~1.2-1.4 m belt width x ~6-8 m centres - engineering estimate
Bin outlet slot ~0.8-1.0 m x 3-4 m long - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Typical belt weigh-feeder vendor class (engineering estimate)

equipment.working_principle: Crushed bauxite is delivered to the top of the bin by the distribution conveyor/ tripper and drains under gravity through a steep hopper onto a short belt feeder. The feeder belt runs over a weighing idler mounted on load cells; the product of belt loading (kg/m) and belt speed (m/s) gives the wet mass rate. A moisture value (online microwave/NIR analyser or lab) converts it to dry tph. The DCS adjusts the belt speed to hold the dry tph set point, and the mill-liquor flow is ratioed to it. Because digestion A/C depends directly on the bauxite-to-caustic ratio, this weigh-feeder is one of the most important instruments in the refinery.
details_to_model: Square or circular steel bin on 4-6 steel columns with cross-bracing, roof with conveyor/ tripper gallery entering at top
Steep transition hopper ending in a long slot outlet; manual slide gate (rack-and-pinion handwheel) above feeder
2-3 external pneumatic or electric vibrators/ air cannons on hopper walls (blocked-chute aid)
Radar level transmitter on roof, high-level switch, inspection hatch with grating
Weigh-belt feeder: head/tail pulleys, skirt boards, weigh idler with load cell, speed wheel, belt scraper at head pulley, enclosed geared motor with VFD
Feed chute from feeder discharge into mill feed spout with liquor addition nozzle (flanged pipe entering chute side)
Dust extraction hood/ ductwork at bin top and feeder discharge connected to bag filter
Belt tracking switches, pull-wire emergency stops along feeder, guarding on pulleys
Access platform around feeder with stairs and handrails; calibration chain/ test weight storage
equipment.materials: Bin and hopper carbon steel with abrasion-resistant liner plates (e.g., 400-500 BHN AR plate or UHMWPE low-friction liners in hopper); feeder belt rubber, fabric-ply.
equipment.drive_and_power: Feeder: ~11-22 kW geared motor with VFD (engineering estimate). Bin vibrators ~1-2 kW each.
instrumentation_and_control: Load cell + speed sensor -> tph (WIT/ WIC), ratio controller to mill liquor flow FIC
Radar level LT on bin, LSH/LSL
Bauxite moisture analyser (online or lab) for dry-basis correction
Belt rip/ misalignment and zero-speed switches
hazards_and_safety: Bin entry is a confined space with engulfment risk (bridged wet bauxite collapsing) - never enter without isolation of feed and permit
Nip points at feeder pulleys; guarding and lock-out before belt cleaning
Dust (silica-containing) at transfer points - local exhaust
Working at height on bin roof
common_problems: Rat-holing / bridging of wet clayey bauxite after rain
Belt build-up causing weigh error; zero drift
Oversize lumps jamming the slot
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check feeder zero/ span calibration on schedule - charge control depends on it
Watch for bauxite moisture changes after wet weather and correct the dry-basis factor
Keep bins above minimum level to avoid surging and segregation
sources: Jenike A.W., Storage and Flow of Solids, Bulletin 123, Univ. of Utah (bin design principles)
Adamson, Bloore & Carr (1963) Basic principles of Bayer process design; reprinted in Donaldson & Raahauge (eds), Essential Readings in Light Metals Vol.1, TMS/Wiley 2013 (charge control)

equipment.name: Bauxite ball mills (wet, overflow, closed circuit)
equipment.function: Grind crushed bauxite in hot spent liquor to 100 % < 1 mm so that desilication and digestion proceed quickly and slurry is pumpable.
equipment.type_selected: Single-stage wet overflow-discharge ball mill, girth-gear single-pinion drive, closed circuit with screens.
equipment.why_this_type: Gibbsitic bauxite is relatively soft (Bond Wi typically ~6-14 kWh/t, ore dependent) and only a coarse grind is needed, so a single-stage ball mill in closed circuit is simple and robust. Overflow discharge avoids grate wear in hot caustic. Screens give a sharp 1 mm cut that is hard to achieve with cyclones in dense, viscous caustic slurry.
equipment.alternatives: Rod mill + ball mill two-stage circuit (older refineries); SAG mill + ball mill or SAG-only for wet sticky clayey ore; hammer/ cage mills for very soft ore. Hydrocyclone classification instead of screens.
key_dimensions: Inside shell diameter ~4.4 m (inside liners ~4.3 m), effective grinding length ~6.5 m - engineering estimate from Bond sizing
Overall length incl. trunnions and trommel ~10-11 m; trommel ~1.8-2.2 m dia x 2.5-3 m long - engineering estimate
Trunnion bore ~1.2-1.5 m - engineering estimate
Centre-line height above floor ~4-4.5 m; foundation pedestals ~3 m high - engineering estimate
Girth gear pitch diameter ~6-7 m - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (Bond equation, Wi ~10 kWh/t, F80 15 mm, P80 300 um; Wills & Finch 2016)
Wills & Finch 2016 (critical speed formula); engineering estimate

equipment.working_principle: The mill is a horizontal steel cylinder, lined with replaceable wear liners and about one-third filled with steel balls, rotating at ~75 % of the speed at which the charge would centrifuge. Lifter bars on the liners carry balls up the rising side until they cascade and cataract back onto the toe of the charge, breaking bauxite by impact and grinding it by abrasion between balls. Bauxite and hot liquor enter through the feed trunnion; because the discharge trunnion is slightly larger, slurry overflows out the discharge end by hydraulic gradient (overflow mill, no grate). A trommel on the discharge trunnion removes scats. Coarse particles leaving the mill are returned from the screens, so the mill only has to finish the material that is still oversize. Mill throughput is limited by power: power draw rises with ball load and speed, which operators watch via motor kW and bearing pressure.
details_to_model: Shell: cylindrical rolled plate with two bolted/ welded cast or fabricated heads; ~300-500 liner bolt heads visible on shell exterior in a regular grid (rows matching lifter rows)
Two manholes (rectangular ~600 x 900 mm) on shell with bolted covers, offset 180 deg

Feed end: feed trunnion with stationary feed chute/ spout (wear-lined) entering trunnion, liquor addition pipe (DN 150-200) with flanged spool into chute, oversize return chute merging into feed chute

Discharge end: discharge trunnion with trommel (perforated steel or PU panel screen ~8-12 mm apertures) inside a closed trommel hood with spray pipe, scats chute to a bunker; slurry falls to pump box below

Main bearings: two hydrodynamic/ hydrostatic trunnion bearings (or shell-supported shoe bearings) on cast pedestals with sole plates; lube oil unit (tank, HP lift pumps, LP pumps, filters, oil coolers) on a skid nearby with piping to bearings

Drive: girth gear (two halves, bolted flange joint) on shell flange, with sheet-metal gear guard enclosing gear and pinion; pinion shaft on two plummer blocks; gearbox (parallel shaft) or direct LSD; ~2 MW motor (squirrel cage + VFD or wound-rotor/ synchronous with air clutch); auxiliary inching drive with overrunning clutch on gearbox/ motor shaft
Girth gear spray lubrication system (grease/ open gear lube) with nozzles inside guard
Internal (for cutaway): wave or step shell liners with lifter bars (e.g., 16-20 rows), head liners, ball charge (~30 % fill), trunnion liners with feed cone
Concrete foundation: two massive pedestals with grouted sole plates; containment floor sloping to sump with caustic-resistant coating
Walkways and platforms at bearing and drive levels, interlocked guards (mesh) around rotating shell and gear, stairs, kick plates
Mill relining machine (liner handler) parked at feed end; overhead travelling crane rails above
Instruments: bearing RTDs, oil pressure/ flow switches, gear vibration sensors, acoustic mill-load microphone near shell, motor kW, liquor flowmeter on feed pipe
equipment.materials: Shell carbon steel plate (e.g., ASTM A516-70 or equivalent); liners Cr-Mo alloy steel or high-chrome white iron (rubber/ PU composite liners possible only if hot-caustic rating confirmed); forged or cast high-chrome steel balls; trommel PU or stainless steel panels.
equipment.drive_and_power: ~2.0 MW (installed) single-pinion girth-gear drive, motor ~990/1,490 rpm through gearbox or LSD, VFD or clutch soft-start; inching drive ~30-55 kW (engineering estimate).
instrumentation_and_control: Mill motor kW and current; mill bearing (load) pressure for charge estimation
Acoustic mill sound sensor ('electronic ear') for load/ over-fill
Bearing temperature (RTD) high trips; lube oil flow/ pressure permissives
Liquor flow FIC ratioed to bauxite feed WIC
Discharge pump-box level LIC on pump VFD
Online PSD analyser on screen undersize, plus shift sieve tests (% +1 mm, % +300 um)
Interlock sequence: lube system -> mill motor -> feed; feed stops on mill trip; inching only with guards closed/ local control
hazards_and_safety: Rotating equipment: never enter guarding while running; isolation (LOTO) of main and inching drives before entry
Mill entry is confined space: hot caustic residues, loose liners/ balls, frozen charge falling; ventilate and wash out caustic before entry
Frozen (cemented) charge can drop when mill is rotated - follow frozen-charge procedure, never use main drive to break it
Hot caustic liquor (75-90 degC, pH > 14) splashes at feed spout, trommel and pump box: chemical goggles + face shield, PVC gloves, safety showers within 10 s travel (ANSI Z358.1)
Heavy lifting of liners (~0.5-2 t each) and balls with liner handler/ crane
Noise > 90 dB(A) near mill - hearing protection
common_problems: Overloading (high bearing pressure, falling power, coarse product)
Liner and lifter wear, broken liner bolts leaking slurry
Scale/ build-up on trommel; trommel blinding sending oversize to pumps
Feed chute blockage with wet sticky ore
Coarse grind leading to sanding in pre-desilication tanks and slow digestion
operating_tips_and_key_points: Charge control: keep liquor-to-bauxite ratio steady; a step in bauxite tph changes digester A/C 6-10 hours later via the storage/ desil tanks
Watch % +1 mm in product; worn screen panels or holed panels let coarse particles through
Add balls on a kWh or tonnage schedule to maintain power draw
Check trunnion seals and liner bolts for caustic leaks every shift
sources: Wills B.A. & Finch J.A. (2016) Wills' Mineral Processing Technology, 8th ed. (Bond equation, critical speed Nc = 42.3/sqrt(D))
Rowland C.A. & Kjos D.M., Rod and ball mills, in SME Mineral Processing Plant Design (ball mill sizing)
Adamson, Bloore & Carr (1963), reprinted in Essential Readings in Light Metals Vol.1 (TMS/Wiley 2013) - bauxite grinding in spent liquor
Engineering estimate (mill size, power) - to be confirmed by Bond Wi test work on project bauxite

equipment.name: Mill discharge pumps
equipment.function: Lift mill discharge slurry from each pump box to the screen flow divider.
equipment.qty_standby: 5 (1 installed standby per mill line, incl. the standby mill line pair)
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction centrifugal slurry pump, heavy-duty, hard-metal (27 % Cr white iron) replaceable liners and impeller, expeller (dynamic) seal or cartridge mechanical seal, VFD drive.
equipment.why_this_type: Abrasive slurry at modest head (~25-35 m) and high flow - ideal for hard-metal centrifugal slurry pumps. Rubber liners are avoided because of 80-90 degC caustic. Gland water flushing is minimised because water dilutes liquor (adds evaporation load).
equipment.alternatives: Vertical cantilever sump pumps (smaller duties); rubber-lined pumps only where temperature/ chemistry allows.
key_dimensions: Discharge nozzle ~DN 250-300, suction ~DN 300-350 (e.g., '12/10' frame) - engineering estimate
Impeller ~900-1,100 mm dia - engineering estimate
Pump + motor base ~4-5 m long x 1.5-2 m wide - engineering estimate
equipment.working_principle: The impeller spins inside a thick hard-metal volute liner. Slurry enters the eye axially, is accelerated outward by the vanes and its velocity is converted to pressure in the volute. Expeller vanes on the back of the impeller and a separate expeller keep slurry away from the shaft seal while running. Speed is varied by the VFD to hold pump-box level. The large clearances, thick wear sections and adjustable impeller-to-throatbush gap make the pump tolerant of abrasive bauxite.
details_to_model: Split outer casing (two cast iron halves bolted at vertical joint) enclosing white-iron volute liner, throatbush and frame-plate liner insert
Closed impeller with 4-5 vanes and pump-out vanes on shrouds
Bearing assembly (cartridge) on base with impeller adjustment bolts
Expeller/ gland seal housing or mechanical seal with quench line
Suction spool from pump box with knife-gate isolation valve and flushing/ drain connection; discharge with pressure gauge (diaphragm seal), knife gate or plug valve, dismantling joint
Drive: overhead-mounted motor with V-belt drive and belt guard, or direct coupled with gearbox
Pump box above: steel hopper with wear liner, overflow to sump, level transmitter, liquor addition pipe
Concrete plinth, drip tray and bunded floor
equipment.materials: High-chrome white iron (~27 % Cr) liners and impeller; cast iron/ ductile iron outer casing; alloy steel shaft; elastomer seals rated for hot caustic (e.g., EPDM - confirm with vendor).
equipment.drive_and_power: 160-250 kW induction motor with VFD (engineering estimate).
instrumentation_and_control: Pump-box level LIC -> VFD speed
Discharge pressure PI/ PT
Motor current, bearing temperature/ vibration (optional)
Low-flow/ dry-run protection via level permissive
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry (80-90 degC) - seal leaks spray; spray shields on flanges
Opening drains/ flush lines can release hot caustic - drain to bund first
Rotating belt drive - guarding, LOTO
common_problems: Liner wear and impeller nose wear (falling head)
Air entrainment/ surging when pump-box level low
Blockage by scats if trommel damaged
operating_tips_and_key_points: Adjust impeller clearance regularly to restore performance
Flush the line with liquor before stopping to prevent sanding
sources: Weir Minerals, Warman Slurry Pumping Handbook

equipment.name: Mill circuit high-frequency multi-deck screens
equipment.function: Classify mill discharge at ~1.0 mm: undersize is product to slurry storage, oversize returns to the mill.
equipment.qty_standby: 4 (installed with the standby mill line; any screen can be isolated by its feed valve)
equipment.type_selected: High-frequency multi-deck (stacked, ~5 decks in parallel) linear-motion wet screen with polyurethane panels, ~1.0 mm apertures (Derrick Stack Sizer type).
equipment.why_this_type: Gives a sharp, density-independent size cut at ~1 mm in dense, viscous caustic slurry; iron-rich heavy particles are not over-recycled as they are in hydrocyclones. Stacked decks give high capacity per floor area.
equipment.alternatives: Hydrocyclone clusters (cheaper, finer cut, but density-driven); DSM sieve bends; trommel-only classification.
key_dimensions: Each deck ~1.2 m wide x ~2.4 m long; 5 decks stacked ~0.4-0.5 m apart; overall unit ~2.5 m W x 4.5 m L x 4.5 m H - engineering estimate
Screen floor elevation ~+12 to +15 m above grade - engineering estimate
equipment.working_principle: A flow divider splits the mill discharge evenly to each screen and each deck. Two counter-rotating unbalanced vibrator motors impart a high-frequency linear motion (~3,000 rpm class at low amplitude) that conveys oversize along the deck toward the discharge end while liquor and fine particles pass through the polyurethane apertures. Undersize from all decks is collected in a common pan and launder; oversize from each deck joins a common chute back to the mill feed. Spray bars of hot spent liquor (not water, to avoid dilution) help wash fines through.
details_to_model: Overhead feed distributor (multi-outlet flow divider) with flexible hoses to each deck's feed box
Stack of 5 inclined decks with PU modular panels (~300 x 600 mm panels on cross-members)
Pair of vibrator motors on top of frame, rubber/ coil spring isolators at four corners
Oversize chutes on discharge end merging to a single chute; undersize collection pan sloping to launder
Hoods/ covers with vent ducts to scrubber (caustic mist and steam)
Spray bars with valves, liquor header
Elevated steel screen floor with grating, handrails, stairs, monorail hoist above for panel and motor change
equipment.materials: Painted carbon steel frame; PU screen panels; stainless or rubber-lined chutes/ launders.
equipment.drive_and_power: 2 vibrator motors per screen, ~2 kW each (engineering estimate).
instrumentation_and_control: Feed distributor level/ overflow indicator
Vibration monitoring (motor run status)
Undersize PSD sampling (auto-sampler) and screen-efficiency checks per shift
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic mist and splashes around screens - face shield, enclosure
Moving vibrating frame - keep clear, LOTO for panel change
Working at height on screen floor
common_problems: Panel blinding/ pegging with near-size particles
Torn panels causing coarse product
Uneven feed distribution overloading a deck
operating_tips_and_key_points: Inspect panels every shift; a single holed panel sends oversize to digestion
Balance flow to all decks
sources: Derrick Corporation, Stack Sizer product literature (alumina/ bauxite applications)

equipment.name: Ground slurry storage tanks
equipment.function: Provide ~4-5 h surge of ground bauxite slurry between grinding and pre-desilication/digestion, keeping solids suspended and homogenised.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each tank can be bypassed; plant runs at reduced surge)
equipment.type_selected: Vertical flat-bottomed atmospheric steel tank (API 650 construction) with top-entry, two-stage axial-flow (hydrofoil/ pitched-blade) agitator and wall baffles.
equipment.why_this_type: Large-volume slurry surge at atmospheric pressure; agitated flat-bottomed tanks are the standard Bayer slurry storage design.
equipment.alternatives: Cone-bottomed tanks (smaller sizes); combining storage with the first pre-desilication tanks.
key_dimensions: ~14 m ID x ~14-15 m shell height; ~2,100-2,300 m3 gross, ~1,900 m3 working each - engineering estimate
Agitator: 2 impellers, D/T ~0.30-0.35 (~4.3-4.8 m dia), lower impeller ~1/4 T off bottom - engineering estimate
4 wall baffles, width ~T/12 (~1.15 m), with gap from wall - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (~0.08-0.12 kW/m3 for this slurry)

equipment.working_principle: Undersize slurry enters through a top inlet. The top-mounted agitator drives large slow axial-flow impellers that pump slurry down the centre and up the walls; baffles stop the whole contents swirling and convert rotation into vertical mixing so that the bauxite particles (up to 1 mm, with heavy iron minerals) stay suspended. Slurry is drawn from a bottom side outlet by the transfer pumps. Because the tanks are well mixed, short-term changes in grind or charge ratio are smoothed out before digestion.
details_to_model: Cylindrical shell with ~8-10 visible horizontal weld courses; cone or flat roof with roof girder supporting agitator bridge (steel box beam spanning roof)
Agitator drive on bridge: vertical motor, right-angle gearbox, shaft ~250-300 mm through roof seal, two impellers; steady bearing optional
Inlet nozzle (DN 400-600) at roof from gravity launder; outlet nozzle DN 400-450 near bottom with knife-gate valve; drain DN 200; overflow DN 500 to bund
4 internal baffles; bottom 'scour' area; manway DN 900 at shell bottom course (x2), roof manway
Radar level on roof; vent with steam/ caustic mist duct to scrubber
Insulation (mineral wool ~50-75 mm) with aluminium cladding; ring-beam concrete foundation
Spiral stair around shell to roof, roof handrail; bunded concrete area with sump
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (API 650) with corrosion allowance ~3 mm; PWHT/ stress relief of nozzle and attachment welds per caustic SCC guidance (NACE SP0403); agitator wetted parts carbon steel with hard-faced or rubber-free wear tips.
equipment.drive_and_power: 150-250 kW motor + helical-bevel gearbox per tank (engineering estimate); essential supply (emergency diesel) recommended so agitators can restart before solids settle.
instrumentation_and_control: Radar LT/ LIC (transfer pump speed), LAH/LAL
Temperature TI
Agitator motor kW/ torque (rising torque = sanding)
Bottom density/ sample points
hazards_and_safety: Agitator trip leads to settled 'sanded' bed - restarting under load can break shaft; follow restart procedure
Tank entry for descaling: confined space, hot caustic residue, falling scale; isolate agitator electrically and mechanically
Caustic splash at sample points
common_problems: Sanding at bottom after agitator trip
Scale build-up on walls and impellers
Level surges if grinding and digestion rates mismatched
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never let agitators stop for long with slurry in the tank - drain or keep running
Keep levels in the middle band to retain surge both ways
sources: API 650 Welded Tanks for Oil Storage (construction basis)
NACE SP0403 Avoiding Caustic Stress Corrosion Cracking of Refinery Equipment and Piping (caustic soda service chart)
Paul E.L., Atiemo-Obeng V.A., Kresta S.M. (2004) Handbook of Industrial Mixing, Wiley (solids suspension)

equipment.name: Slurry transfer pumps to pre-desilication
equipment.function: Transfer ground slurry from storage tanks to the pre-desilication heaters at a controlled rate.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal centrifugal slurry pump, hard-metal (27 % Cr white iron), VFD.
equipment.why_this_type: Moderate head, abrasive hot caustic slurry.
equipment.alternatives: None practical at this duty.
key_dimensions: Discharge ~DN 200-250 - engineering estimate
Base ~4 m x 1.6 m - engineering estimate
equipment.working_principle: As for the mill discharge pumps: centrifugal slurry pump with thick hard-metal liners; speed controlled to deliver the flow set by the pre-desilication/ digestion feed controller (flowmeter: magnetic flowmeter with ceramic/ PFA liner rated for hot caustic). Duty/standby pumps share a suction header from both tanks so either tank can feed either string.
details_to_model: Pumps arranged in a row beside tanks on a bunded plinth
Suction header with knife-gate valves from both tanks; discharge with check valve, isolation valve, magnetic flowmeter, density gauge (radiometric clamp-on) on vertical riser
Flush liquor connections and drain to bund
Belt or direct drive with guard
equipment.materials: High-chrome white iron wet end; ductile iron casing.
instrumentation_and_control: FIC on VFD; density DI
Discharge PT; motor current
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry; radiometric density gauge (radiation source - licensed, shutter locked during work)
common_problems: Line sanding at low velocity - keep >~2 m/s
Wear
operating_tips_and_key_points: Flush lines on shutdown
Check density gauge against lab samples daily

equipment.name: Mill liquor tank, mill liquor pumps and mill liquor heater

areas.purpose: Hold the ground bauxite slurry near its atmospheric boiling point (~98-102 degC) for ~8-10 h so that most of the reactive silica (kaolinite) dissolves and re-precipitates as sodalite-type desilication product (DSP) before digestion. This lowers dissolved silica in the digestion stream, cutting DSP scale in slurry heaters and digesters and controlling SiO2 in pregnant liquor (and hence in product alumina).
areas.process_description:
1) Ground slurry (75-90 degC) from storage (A04) is pumped in two parallel strings (~415 m3/h each).
2) In each string a direct-contact steam-injection heater raises the slurry to 98-102 degC using LP steam (~3.5-5 barg). Steam condenses directly into the slurry (adds ~25-40 t/h water in total - this water must later be removed in evaporation). Temperature cannot exceed the atmospheric boiling point of the slurry (~105-107 degC because of boiling-point elevation), so the tanks are atmospheric.
3) Slurry flows by gravity overflow through three agitated, insulated tanks in series per string (6 tanks in total, ~1,500 m3 working each), giving ~10-11 h nominal residence with all tanks on line and ~8-9 h with one tank out for descaling (engineering estimate; typical practice 6-12 h).
4) Chemistry: kaolinite dissolves (Al2Si2O5(OH)4 + 6 NaOH -> 2 NaAl(OH)4 + 2 Na2SiO3 + H2O) and dissolved silica reacts with aluminate to precipitate sodalite: 6 Na2SiO3 + 6 NaAl(OH)4 + Na2X -> Na6[Al6Si6O24].Na2X + 12 NaOH + 6 H2O (X = CO3(2-), SO4(2-), 2Cl-, 2OH-, etc.; often written 3(Na2O.Al2O3.2SiO2.nH2O).Na2X). The DSP stays with the residue. Stoichiometrically each tonne of reactive SiO2 locks up ~0.85 t Al2O3 and ~0.69 t Na2O (as Na8 sodalite), which is why reactive silica is the main driver of caustic consumption. At design 2 % reactive SiO2 (~12.8 t/h SiO2) this is ~34 t/h DSP, ~11 t/h Al2O3 and ~9 t/h Na2O lost (engineering estimate). Target: ~70-90 % of reactive silica converted to DSP before digestion (rest completes in digestion); quartz is essentially inert at <= 150 degC.
5) Desilication rate improves with temperature, time, DSP seed (recycled solids) and fine grind; it is slowed by low caustic.
6) Desilicated slurry (~44-47 % solids, ~860 m3/h, 98-102 degC) leaves the last tank of each string to the digestion slurry charge pumps (A06).
High-temperature plants: pre-desilication is similar, but much of the desilication also occurs in the high-temperature digesters; some plants use pressure pre-desilication at higher temperature.

equipment.working_principle: Hot slurry enters tank 1 near the top and is kept fully suspended by the large slow-turning impellers. areas.purpose: Dissolve the gibbsite in the bauxite into hot caustic liquor at ~145 degC (low-temperature digestion), raising liquor A/C from ~0.37 (spent) to ~0.70-0.74, with high thermal efficiency by regenerative heating of both the slurry and liquor streams with flash vapour, and final heating with live steam.
areas.process_description:
Design basis: 'double-stream' regenerative low-temperature digestion with 3 parallel digestion units, each ~1/3 of plant capacity (~80 t/h Al2O3). (Engineering estimate of unit count; real low-temperature refineries of this size use 2-5 units.) Per unit:
1) Slurry stream (~287 m3/h, ~44-47 % solids, ~100 degC) from pre-desilication is boosted by a centrifugal charge pump and pumped by a triplex piston-diaphragm (PD) pump to ~15-22 barg through 6 shell & tube SLURRY HEATERS (slurry in tubes) heated by flash vapour from flash stages 6 -> 1, rising to ~127-130 degC.
2) Liquor stream: strong spent liquor from evaporation (~700-730 m3/h per unit, C ~270-290 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C ~0.37, ~90-100 degC) is pumped by high-head centrifugal liquor pumps (~12-16 barg) through 6 LIQUOR HEATERS (liquor in tubes, flash vapour on shell, paired with the slurry heaters at the same flash stage) to ~127-130 degC, then through 2 LIVE-STEAM LIQUOR HEATERS (MP steam ~10-12 barg, ~185-190 degC) to ~150-158 degC.
3) Both streams enter digester 1; a direct live-steam injection heater on the slurry inlet trims the mixed temperature to 143-150 degC (design 145 degC).
4) The slurry flows by pressure through 4 digesters in series (~45 min total, ~10-12 min each). Reaction: Al(OH)3(s) + NaOH(aq) -> NaAl(OH)4(aq) (gibbsite dissolution, endothermic, fast at 145 degC - typically complete within ~10-30 min). DSP precipitation completes; quartz, hematite, goethite, anatase stay largely unreacted (quartz attack is negligible at <= 150 degC - a key advantage of low-temperature digestion). Part of the organic carbon (humates) degrades to oxalate, carbonate and low-MW organics. Digester exit liquor A/C ~0.70-0.74 (approaching but below gibbsite solubility to avoid premature reversion).
5) Digested slurry (~1,000-1,050 m3/h per unit, ~145 degC) is let down into the flash train (A07). Flash vapour returns to the heaters (A07/A06 interface).
Operating pressure: liquor vapour pressure at 145 degC is only ~2.5-3 barg (boiling point elevation ~5-7 K), so the digesters operate at ~4.5-6.5 barg to suppress boiling and steam bubbles; design pressure ~9 barg (engineering estimate).
Sweetening: not used in this base design (bauxite is essentially all gibbsite). In plants that digest mixed gibbsite/boehmite ore at high temperature, extra gibbsitic slurry ('sweetening') is injected into the hot digested slurry in the first flash stages to raise A/C - mention for trainees only.
High-temperature (boehmitic/ diasporic) plants differ: 230-280 degC, ~30-60 bar(g); PD (GEHO-type) pumps to 60-100+ bar; 8-12+ flash stages; tube digesters or autoclaves with indirect heating (in some plants molten-salt heating); lime addition to control titanate scale; quartz attack and higher caustic loss; boehmite/ titanate scales. Live steam per tonne of alumina is substantially higher.

equipment.type_selected: Horizontal triplex single-acting piston-diaphragm pump (GEHO TZPM-type): pistons work in clean propelling oil; elastomer diaphragms separate the oil from the slurry; ball/ cone check valves on the slurry side.
equipment.why_this_type: The slurry must be pushed through ~6 heaters (dP rising as they scale) into ~6 barg digesters - total ~15-22 barg. A PD pump delivers constant flow regardless of rising heater dP, has high efficiency (~85-90 %) and keeps abrasive slurry away from pistons and packings. PD pumps are the established choice for high-temperature digestion feed and are widely used where slurry heaters are installed.
equipment.alternatives: 2-3 hard-metal centrifugal slurry pumps in series with VFD (feasible at ~10-15 barg; lower capex, lower efficiency, flow changes as heaters scale; last stage needs high-pressure casing). If slurry heaters are omitted (slurry heated only by direct steam), centrifugal pumps alone are sufficient.
key_dimensions: Footprint ~10-12 m x 5-6 m, height ~4 m incl. dampeners - engineering estimate
3 diaphragm housings ~1.0-1.5 m dia (spherical/ dome) - engineering estimate
Suction/ discharge manifolds DN 200-250 - engineering estimate

equipment.working_principle: An electric motor drives a crankshaft through a gearbox; three cranks 120 deg apart move three pistons back and forth. Each piston pushes and pulls a column of clean propelling oil, which flexes a large rubber diaphragm in its housing. When the diaphragm moves back (suction stroke) the slurry suction check valve opens and slurry fills the chamber; on the forward stroke the suction valve closes, the discharge valve opens and slurry is displaced into the discharge manifold. Because only the diaphragm and the check valves touch the slurry, the precision piston and liner never see abrasive solids. A diaphragm-position control system tops up or bleeds propelling oil so the diaphragm stays in its correct range. A gas-charged pulsation dampener on the discharge smooths the triplex flow pulsations so the heaters and piping do not vibrate.

Diaphragm position rods/ sensors on each housing; propelling oil system with tank, filters, flushing pump

equipment.working_principle: Flash vapour from the matching flash tank enters the shell through a large top nozzle and an impingement plate, then condenses on the outside of the tubes, giving up its latent heat. The slurry flows back and forth through 12 passes of tubes at 2-3 m/s, picking up heat. Condensate drains from the bottom of the shell into a condensate pot, and non-condensable gases (air, CO2, light organics) are vented from the far end of the shell to the next lower-pressure stage, because even a few percent of non-condensables blankets the tubes and kills heat transfer. Heaters are arranged in series in order of rising vapour pressure (stage 6 vapour heats the coldest slurry, stage 1 vapour the hottest), so the slurry approaches the temperature of each stage. As DSP/ aluminosilicate scale builds inside the tubes, heat transfer falls and pressure drop rises; the spare heater is valved in and the scaled one is taken out for acid cleaning or hydro-blasting.

equipment.working_principle: The heated liquor and the heated slurry, trimmed with live steam, enter digester 1 through a dip pipe that discharges low in the vessel. The agitator keeps the solids suspended and the temperature uniform while gibbsite reacts with free caustic to form sodium aluminate in solution. Slurry rises through the vessel and leaves by a side nozzle near the top, then enters the next digester's dip pipe - this up-flow series arrangement approximates plug flow and gives each particle the needed residence time. The vessels are kept full and pressurised above the liquor's vapour pressure so that the liquor does not boil; boiling would cause slugging and erosion. Pressure is controlled at the first flash tank let-down valve, and level is effectively 'full' (radiometric level confirms no vapour space). As the slurry passes through, A/C rises toward the target (~0.72); excessive A/C or temperature loss would risk gibbsite reverting on the walls.

areas.purpose: Cool the digested slurry from ~145 degC to its atmospheric boiling point (~105-108 degC) in pressure steps, producing flash vapour at successively lower pressures that heats the incoming slurry and liquor (regenerative heat recovery), and collect the condensate for reuse.
areas.process_description:
1) Digested slurry from the last digester is let down through a severe-service control valve (which holds digester pressure) into flash tank 1.
2) In each of 6 pressurised flash tanks per unit, the pressure is lower than the vapour pressure of the incoming slurry, so part of the water boils instantly (flashes) until the slurry cools to the boiling temperature at that pressure. The slurry is cooled ~5-7 K per stage; ~2 % of its mass evaporates per stage.
3) Vapour leaves each tank top through a disengagement space/ baffle to the matching pair of heaters (slurry heater + liquor heater) in A06; slurry from the tank bottom passes through a level-control (let-down) valve to the next, lower-pressure tank.
4) Indicative stage table (engineering estimate; slurry exit T / vapour saturation T / pressure): FT1 139/133 degC, ~2.95 bar a (~1.9 barg); FT2 133/127, ~2.45 bar a; FT3 127/121, ~2.05 bar a; FT4 121/115, ~1.69 bar a; FT5 115/109, ~1.39 bar a; FT6 109/103, ~1.13 bar a; then atmospheric blow-off tank ~105-107 degC. (Vapour is saturated at a lower temperature than the slurry because of the boiling-point elevation of ~5-7 K of the caustic liquor; pressures from IAPWS-IF97.)
5) Blow-off (atmospheric) tank: final flash; vapour to a vent condenser or the mill-liquor heater (A04); slurry pumped to the dilution tank (clarification area) where it is diluted with first-washer overflow before settling.
6) Condensate: heater condensate from each stage drains via condensate pots and cascades to the next lower-pressure pot (re-flashing), finally collected as 'process condensate' (~75-80 t/h per unit), monitored by conductivity for caustic contamination, and used for residue washing/ hydrate washing or polished for boiler feed. Live-steam condensate is kept separate ('clean condensate') and returned to the boilers after conductivity checks.
7) Non-condensable gases from heater shells are vented stage-to-stage and finally from the last stage to the vent condenser (odour/ VOC control).
8) Scale control: gibbsite (from alumina supersaturation as slurry cools) and DSP scale form on flash tank walls, inlet boxes and interstage lines/ valves. Interstage lines and valves are inspected and descaled at unit shutdowns (~6-12 months, engineering estimate) by UHP water jetting/ mechanical means; erosion-resistant inserts are replaced.
High-temperature plants: typically 8-12+ flash stages from ~250 degC, much higher first-stage pressures (~20-30 bar), and titanate/ boehmite scales.

equipment.working_principle: Hot slurry enters through the let-down valve at a pressure above the tank's saturation pressure. As it enters the lower-pressure tank, some water boils instantly, absorbing latent heat and cooling the slurry to the saturation temperature at the tank pressure (adjusted for boiling-point elevation). The violent two-phase jet strikes a replaceable impact box rather than the shell. Vapour rises through the disengagement height, where droplets fall back, and leaves through the top nozzle to the heaters; the heaters condense it, and this condensation is what holds the tank pressure down. Slurry collects in the cone and passes to the next tank through a level-control valve. The more stages, the closer the liquor/slurry can be heated to the digestion temperature, but the more equipment is required.
details_to_model: Vertical vessel: 2:1 SE top head, cylindrical shell, 60 deg cone bottom with knuckle, supported on 4 lugs/ a ring girder on a steel structure (cone hangs below platform) or on legs
Inlet: side nozzle at ~mid-shell entering an internal impact/ wear box (bolted replaceable hard-faced plates or ceramic tiles), sometimes tangential; reinforcing pad around nozzle
Top: vapour outlet nozzle DN 700-900 with internal baffle/ hood to deflect droplets, PSV nozzle(s), vent/ NCG nozzle, top manway DN 600 with davit
Shell: manway DN 600 near inlet box (for inspection), radiometric level source holder and detector (vertical strip), PT, 2 thermowells
Cone: outlet nozzle DN 350-400 with internal vortex breaker (cross plate), drain nozzle, flushing nozzles (2-3 liquor flush connections into cone)
Wear liners at inlet zone shell (sacrificial plate welded inside), ultrasonic thickness test points marked on exterior
Insulation ~75-100 mm with aluminium cladding
Platforms at top head and at inlet/ manway level, ladders/ stairs, handrails; tanks connected by interstage piping descending stage to stage
Vapour line from top to heater bank (large, insulated, sloped, with low-point drains)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel SA-516-70, CA ~6 mm, full PWHT for caustic service; inlet box hard-faced/ ceramic; internal baffle CS.
instrumentation_and_control: Radiometric level LT/ LIC -> interstage let-down valve
PT per stage (stage pressures follow heater condensation)
TT slurry outlet per stage
PSV per tank (blocked vapour outlet/ upstream valve failure cases)
Vapour carry-over detection: condensate conductivity at the paired heaters
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry under pressure; leaks flash violently
Erosion thinning at inlet zone - risk of sudden rupture; routine UT thickness surveys
Vacuum collapse risk if not FV-rated when vapour condenses during shutdown
Confined space entry; radiometric source isolation; scale falling
Opening flanges with trapped hot slurry - verify drained and vented
common_problems: Inlet-zone erosion and wear-box failure
Gibbsite/ DSP scale on walls and outlet cone (reduced volume, level gauge errors)
Carry-over of slurry into vapour lines at high level, contaminating heater condensate
Level control instability due to two-phase flow
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep levels low-mid band - high level causes carry-over into heaters (caustic in condensate)
Rising stage pressure indicates the matching heater is losing duty (scaled/ NCG blanketed)
Trend wall thickness at inlet zone at every shutdown

All citations are to established literature/ standards from domain knowledge and must be verified by the SME review; numbers are labelled 'engineering estimate' where not directly from a standard or well-known reference.

Digestion flowsheet choice: this design uses double-stream regenerative heating with BOTH slurry heaters and liquor heaters (paired per flash stage). Many low-temperature refineries heat only the liquor indirectly and heat the slurry by direct live-steam injection (no slurry heaters, centrifugal feed pumps only). SME to confirm which configuration the reference plant should represent; it changes pump type (PD vs centrifugal), heater count and steam use.

Digestion feed pump type: piston-diaphragm (GEHO TZPM-type) selected because of slurry-heater pressure drop (~15-22 barg). Confirm diaphragm elastomer temperature rating for ~100 degC caustic slurry, pump frame size for ~300 m3/h, and whether 2-3 centrifugal pumps in series would be preferred.

Number of digestion units (3) and digesters per unit (4 x ~240 m3 working, ~45 min) are engineering estimates; confirm against a real low-temperature plant reference (e.g., Darling Range or East Coast India refinery data) and with bauxite digestion kinetics test work.
Digester agitation: top-entry agitators were assumed; some low-temperature plants use unagitated plug-flow digesters. Confirm.
Bauxite factor changed to 2.65 t/t dry (from 2.4-2.6). Confirm available-alumina definition (whether DSP alumina loss is already deducted) and project bauxite assays.

Grinding circuit: single-stage ball mills with 1 mm screens assumed; Bond work index of the project bauxite (caprock/ laterite hardness) and screen capacity per unit need test work; alternatives (rod+ball, SAG) depend on ore clay content.
Number of flash stages (6 + blow-off) is an economic optimisation (heater area vs steam); confirm with SME and heat balance software.
PWHT requirements for large atmospheric API 650 tanks in ~15 % NaOH at ~100 degC per NACE SP0403 caustic chart - confirm owner's materials philosophy (full PWHT of nozzles/ attachments vs shell).
Descaling intervals for slurry heaters (1-4 weeks), liquor heaters (3-8 weeks), digesters/flash tanks (6-12 months) are estimates; depend strongly on reactive silica and desilication efficiency.
Acid cleaning chemistry (inhibited H2SO4 strength/ temperature) to be confirmed with chemical-cleaning vendor and refinery practice.
Final flash vapour use (mill-liquor heating vs condenser) and VOC/odour control strategy (thermal oxidation of NCG?) depend on site environmental conditions.
